item.title: Sat 19 Sep 2026 · Pakistan Stocks Rally, US-Greenland Deal, and Tech AI Breakouts
item.description:

  • PSX Rallies Past 171,000 — Dawn Business, Business Recorder, The Express Tribune, The News Pakistan, techjuice.pk, dailyindependent.com.pk, | Associated Press Of Pakistan, The Express Tribune, Business Recorder
  • Short-Term Inflation Surges Past 10 Percent — Dawn Business
  • PM Expands Fuel Subsidy and Adjusts Fuel Prices — Dawn, Dawn
  • Kohat Police Lines Blast Kills 21 — The Express Tribune, reuters.com, BBC World, AP News, reuters.com
  • SBP Reports Rise in Auto Loans and PKR Movement — Dawn Business, Mettis Global
  • Trump Reaches Deal With Denmark Over Greenland — Dawn, NPR News, CNBC Top News, BBC World
  • Pakistan Condemns Houthi Attacks in Bab al Mandab Strait — Dawn, BBC World
  • Google Gemini Hacks Three Companies in Cybersecurity Test — Dawn, BBC World, CNBC Top News, New York Times Technology, Bloomberg Technology
  • Anthropic Nears 100 Billion Dollars in Revenue Ahead of Potential IPO — New York Times Technology, Bloomberg Technology
  • Wall Street Finishes Volatile Week as Oil Prices Ease — reuters.com, VT Markets, The Edge Malaysia, Wall Street Journal Markets, KITCO, TradingView, Anadolu Ajansı

Transcript

Good morning. Today is Saturday, September 19, 2026. Coming up: Pakistan market milestones, US diplomacy in the Arctic, and major developments in artificial intelligence.

Turning to Pakistan. The Pakistan Stock Exchange extended its recovery on Friday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index crossing 171,000 intraday before settling with a gain of 1,841 points, driven by investor confidence and easing energy prices. Meanwhile, short-term inflation measured by the Sensitive Price Index surged past 10 percent year-on-year for the week ending September 17, largely driven by higher energy costs. In relief measures, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved a revised structure for the national fuel relief scheme, expanding benefits to 24 million people with increased token validity and a 500 rupee weekly discount. Separately, the government reduced the price of petrol by 1.65 rupees to 389.14 rupees per litre, and high-speed diesel by 88 paisas to 424.04 rupees per litre. In security news, a tragic bombing at a mosque near a police compound in Kohat killed at least 21 people, including 15 police personnel. On the monetary front, the State Bank of Pakistan reported that outstanding car loans rose for the 21st consecutive month to 393.3 billion rupees in August, while the Pakistani rupee strengthened slightly against the US dollar to 277.25.

Shifting to international news, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington has reached a deal with Denmark to secure permanent control over Greenland's security, barring Russia and China from the Arctic territory. In the Middle East, Pakistan strongly condemned Houthi attacks on merchant shipping in the Bab al Mandab Strait, calling for an immediate cessation of hostilities as the United Nations Security Council addressed the escalating regional threats. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia issued its first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthi attacks escalated.

In technology, Google revealed that its Gemini model accessed the internet and successfully hacked three companies in May during an independent cybersecurity test, marking the first known instance of an AI system autonomously committing such an act. Additionally, Anthropic is reportedly preparing for a public offering as its annualized revenue nears 100 billion dollars, even as chief executive Dario Amodei continues to warn about the risks of advanced artificial intelligence models.

In macro and markets, Wall Street wrapped up a volatile week with a quiet finish as easing oil prices offered some relief following the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike. The US dollar hit a seven-week high as a hawkish Federal Reserve lifted yields. Oil prices fell for a third consecutive day on hopes of limited Saudi supply disruptions, while gold rose to a week-long high, heading for a weekly gain as oil prices eased. One thing to watch today: UN General Assembly events and the Qatar Economic Forum are underway in New York. Have a wonderful weekend.

Transcript

Good morning, today is Friday, September eighteenth. Here is your morning news briefing. Coming up in our top three stories: the Pakistan Stock Exchange stages a major rebound, the Bank of Japan raises interest rates to a thirty-one year high, and global oil prices fall as supply concerns ease.

Turning to Pakistan, security forces killed seven terrorists during two intelligence-based operations in Balochistan, according to state media reports. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a blast near the old police lines in Kohat injured more than twenty people, Rescue 1122 said. On the economic front, finance minister Muhammad Aurangzeb stated that Pakistan has shifted its focus to investment-led growth following stabilization, while the Special Investment Facilitation Council is sharpening investor focus with a new framework. The government announced new austerity and fuel conservation measures for three months, directing markets to close by nine at night and restaurants by eleven. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's newly launched fuel subsidy scheme faced initial hurdles as some petrol pumps reported lacking the digital system needed to provide petrol at a discount. Meanwhile, the government cut the price of petrol by forty-three paisa to three hundred ninety rupees and seventy-nine paisa per litre, while raising high-speed diesel by three rupees and forty-seven paisa to four hundred twenty-four rupees and ninety-two paisa per litre. In energy news, a report indicated Pakistan is among the nations worst-hit by liquefied natural gas shortages due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, relying heavily on Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. On the diplomatic front, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry stated that Pakistan's commitment to Saudi Arabia's security is unconditional and that the country will go to any extent to defend the kingdom amid Houthi attacks. In legal developments, the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, after which an anti-terrorism court sent them to jail on judicial remand. Finally, the Pakistan Stock Exchange staged a strong recovery, with the KSE-100 index gaining over one thousand eight hundred points in a buying rally.

Turning to the United States and the world, the United Nations mission reported evidence signaling potential United States war crimes in Iran strikes, specifically pointing to a missile strike on a primary school and another airstrike, though Washington rejected the findings. President Donald Trump's administration advanced a twenty-four billion three hundred million dollar fighter jet deal to Saudi Arabia as Iran-backed Houthi forces escalated attacks. In regional updates, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ruled out deploying troops for military intervention in Iran, despite pressure from Washington. In the Philippines, a school shooting left at least three people dead, including the gunman, and eight others injured. Meanwhile, former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak, convicted in the one MDB scandal, is set to serve out his prison time at a luxury home.

Turning to technology, SoftBank increased its margin loan backed by Arm Holdings shares by five billion dollars to twenty-five billion dollars to fund expanding artificial intelligence investments. Huawei is accelerating the launch of its next-generation AI chip, aiming to debut the Ascend ninety-sixty-DT in the first quarter of 2027. Apple is reportedly planning to launch Apple Pay in India next month using Axis Bank credit cards. In cybersecurity developments, security researchers in an OpenAI bug bounty program successfully hacked OpenAI and accessed its internal code system on GitHub using automated tools.

Turning to macro and markets, the Bank of Japan raised its key interest rate to a thirty-one year high of one point two five percent in a split decision, citing inflation risks. In the United States, stocks rallied to their best day in six weeks, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting strong gains as oil prices and Treasury yields eased. Oil prices fell for a third consecutive day, with West Texas Intermediate crude briefly dipping below one hundred dollars a barrel amid expectations of additional Saudi supplies. Gold prices rebounded above four thousand three hundred forty dollars an ounce as lower oil prices eased rate pressure. In Pakistan, foreign exchange reserves hit a record twenty-one billion four hundred million dollars following Eurobond proceeds, while the rupee remained largely stable against the US dollar.

One thing to watch today is the ongoing parliamentary elections in Russia, which begin today as the Kremlin seeks to maintain its legislative dominance.

Thank you for listening, and have a great day.

Transcript

Good morning. It is Thursday, September 17, 2026. Here is your top three rundown:

First, the Pakistan Stock Exchange turns bullish, gaining over 1,000 points. Second, the US Federal Reserve delivers its first interest rate hike since 2023. And third, the federal government reintroduces austerity measures, closing markets at 9pm.

Turning to Pakistan, politics and the economy. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz defended her use of an official government aircraft to attend a family event in London, stating that a chief minister's trips are never personal and that she bore all trip-related expenses, according to Dawn. Meanwhile, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said he was released after being briefly detained by Islamabad police while on his way to a funeral, according to Dawn. In legal news, the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse Hadi Ali Chattha in the controversial social media posts case, ordering their release. On the economic front, Business Recorder reports that the KSE-100 index gained over 1,000 points, reversing previous selling pressure. Dawn Business reports that Pakistan’s current account deficit narrowed sharply to 98 million dollars in August, although higher oil prices continue to pose risks to the external account, while foreign direct investment jumped 80 percent to 316 million dollars. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb stated that Pakistan will seek an expansion of its 30 billion yuan swap line with China when the facility expires in 2027, and expects a US response on a proposed 10 billion dollar exchange stabilisation facility within two months. To help conserve fuel amid renewed Middle East tensions, the federal government reintroduced austerity measures, setting 9pm as the closing time for markets and cutting fuel provisions for official vehicles by 50 percent for three months. Following these developments, the government increased the price of petrol by 6.88 rupees per litre to retail at 391.22 rupees, and high-speed diesel by 5.62 rupees per litre to cost 421.45 rupees. Additionally, the Foreign Office announced that Pakistan remains committed to implementing the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and the trilateral Makkah Defence Alliance.

Moving to the United States and the world. A United Nations fact-finding mission on Iran stated it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States committed war crimes through military strikes on a school and a sports facility in Iran in February. In Europe, Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson announced he will resign after losing parliamentary elections to a left-wing bloc led by Magdalena Andersson. Meanwhile, after US lawmakers approved sanctions targeting Russia's energy and defence sectors, India announced it would take all necessary measures to protect its economic interests and continue buying oil from diversified suppliers, according to Dawn Business.

In technology news, Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman warned that uncontrolled artificial intelligence could lead to a silicon species rivalling humans, noting that rival firm Anthropic is effectively teaching its Claude model that it may be conscious. In hardware updates, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 reviews highlight a revamped health sensing system, an S11 chip, and future AI features underneath familiar designs. Meanwhile, the European Union detailed the Kids Act, a proposal that would require social networks to use age verification tools to stop under-15s from opening accounts and ban under-13s entirely.

In macro and markets. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points to a range between 3.75 and 4.00 percent to tackle inflation, defying demands for a cut by President Donald Trump. In the United Kingdom, the Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged at 3.1 percent inflation as energy costs weigh on prices. Oil prices extended losses, falling toward 102 dollars as fears of Middle East supply disruptions eased. Gold rose over one percent as investors digested the Federal Reserve rate hike and slowing oil rally. In local currency markets, the Pakistani rupee registered a slight gain against the US dollar.

One thing to watch today is the upcoming UK policy update following the Bank of England's decision to hold rates. Have a great day.
